topic: Roger Heard The Poneglyphs But Couldn't Read Like Ohara
title: Roger Heard The Poneglyphs But Couldn't Read Like Ohara
description: Gol D. Roger reached Laugh Tale, but Rayleigh admits his crew were not scholars like the archaeologists of Ohara. What that means for how the Void Century gets read. Is a scholar or a captain the better witness?
comment: Who would you trust more to read the Void Century: Roger's crew or Ohara's scholars?

lines.text: Nobody noticed what Rayleigh admitted about Roger's crew in chapter 507.

shot.fallback: old swordsman with glasses recalling a pirate crew

lines.text: But Rayleigh says Roger found the Poneglyphs because he could hear the voice of all things.

shot.search: Gol D. Roger voice of all things
shot.fallback: captain listening closely to a glowing stone

lines.text: Hearing a stone and reading a stone are not the same skill.

shot.fallback: large dark blue stone covered in carved script

lines.text: Rayleigh even says his crew weren't proper historians, not like the archaeologists of Ohara.

shot.fallback: old swordsman shaking his head gently

lines.text: Gaban's page agrees. Without scholars of that caliber, the crew might have interpreted the truth differently.

shot.search: Scopper Gaban Roger Pirates Void Century
shot.fallback: broad pirate crewman at a ship railing

lines.text: At Sabaody, Rayleigh offered to tell Robin everything, and she turned him down.

shot.fallback: old swordsman speaking to a seated archaeologist

lines.text: My read is that she refused because a second-hand verdict is exactly what Ohara was built to avoid.

shot.fallback: woman running her hand over carved stone

lines.text: People say Roger had Oden, who could read the script. True, and Oden read the Road Poneglyphs.

shot.fallback: samurai pirate reading a stone block

lines.text: But reading a script and interpreting a century are different jobs, and Rayleigh says the truth reads differently from each view.

shot.fallback: old swordsman looking at distant ocean

lines.text: So whose reading of that century was the Government afraid of: Roger's, or the scholars'?

shot.fallback: scholars in a giant tree library

lines.text: And that is the part nobody noticed.

shot.fallback: old swordsman with a quiet smile

self_check.hook: Contrarian first line about Aokiji's real motive.
self_check.loop: Last line hands straight into line 1.
